ownerOnboarding.observed: Synthetic Alice owner signed in, created Billing Console Fixture, and opened /app/billing.

ownerFreeReadback.observed: The owner console displayed TEST MODE, Local · Test, Free inactive, finite usage of 2/3 seats, 0/50 scans, and USD 0.00/USD 0.50 Eve budget.

checkoutApi.observed: Start checkout returned a LocalBillingAdapter session URL and persisted one billing customer mapping.

checkoutFixturePage.observed: The returned /billing/test-checkout URL opened in a new browser tab and rendered Not Found.

portalApi.observed: Manage subscription returned a LocalBillingAdapter portal session URL.

portalFixturePage.observed: The returned /billing/test-portal URL opened in a new browser tab and rendered Not Found.

signedWebhook.observed: A signed raw local fixture POST to /v1/billing/webhook returned HTTP 200 and applied an active Team subscription; no live provider was contacted.

ownerVerifiedEntitlement.observed: After reload, the owner console displayed Team Active, Webhooks Verified, 3/10 seats, 0/750 scans, USD 0.00/USD 5.00 Eve budget, and 10.0 GB stored-bytes allowance.

persistence.observed: PostgreSQL held one billing customer, subscription, webhook event, and usage row; the webhook was handled; Better Auth held owner and reader members; seats rose from 2 to 3 after reader invitation acceptance.

readerDenial.observed: Ben reader accepted an invitation; the overview exposed no company-admin section, and direct /app/billing rendered server denial 'Owner or admin access is required for company billing.' with no checkout or portal controls.

browserConsole.observed: No browser warning or error logs were observed in the billing, checkout, or portal tabs.

defects.observed: Both URLs returned by ready local checkout and portal actions are unhandled by the composed runtime and render HTTP 404 Not Found.
defects.scope: local test harness/runtime route; this does not claim a live Stripe failure

limits: Local synthetic identity and LocalBillingAdapter only; no Stripe account, live provider, remote customer, product, price, charge, or real payment method.
The signed fixture webhook was sent programmatically with an ephemeral test secret; it proves local webhook verification and persistence only.
The 404 hosted fixture pages remain open, so this record does not establish commercial launch or paid readiness.
Screenshots were rendered by CUA, but the connected browser backend did not provide screenshot file export.
